chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm al-Rizzāmī narrated to me from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام.
He عليه السلام said: “The person most entitled to the deceased should wash the dead body.”
And (1377) 22 — Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār said:

I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام: What is the limit of the water with which the deceased is washed, as they have narrated that “the junub performs ghusl with six arṭāl and the menstruating woman with nine arṭāl”? So is there a set limit for the deceased regarding the water with which he is washed? He عليه السلام wrote: “The limit of the ghusl of the deceased is that he is washed until he becomes pure, if Allah, Most High, wills.”
I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام: Is it permissible for the deceased to be washed while the water poured over him enters into the pit of a privy? He عليه السلام wrote: “That should be in drains.”

key_terms.أَرْطَالٍ: a measure of weight or volume used for water quantity
key_terms.أَوْلَى: the one with the strongest priority or greatest right
key_terms.الْجُنُبَ: a person in the state requiring ghusl due to major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person whose body is to be washed
key_terms.غُسْلِ: ritual washing, here specifically the washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: Who should wash the deceased, and is there a fixed amount of water for ghusl al-mayyit?
ai.summary: These narrations address legal rulings concerning the ghusl of the deceased in Shia fiqh. They state that the one most entitled to the deceased should perform the washing, that no fixed amount of water is required so long as cleansing is achieved, and that the drainage of the wash-water should be directed into proper drains.
